title_en: Liu Danping v. Nanjing Renchuang Materials Co., Ltd. — labor dispute
ruling_gist_en: Where an employer fails to sign a written labor contract with the person in charge of human resources (HR supervisor), and the HR supervisor sues the employer for double wage compensation due to the failure to sign a written labor contract, since signing a written labor contract is part of the HR supervisor's job duties, the HR supervisor has an obligation to remind the employer to sign a written labor contract with him/her. If the HR supervisor fails to provide evidence that he/she once reminded the employer to sign a written labor contract with him/her, then the claim should not be upheld.

full_text_en:
Liu Danping v. Nanjing Renchuang Materials Co., Ltd.

— labor dispute

Ruling Summary

Where an employer fails to conclude a written labor contract with its personnel manager, and the personnel manager claims compensation for double wages due to the failure to conclude a written labor contract, since the conclusion of a written labor contract falls within the scope of the personnel manager's job duties, the personnel manager has the obligation to remind the employer to conclude a written labor contract with him/her. If the personnel manager fails to provide evidence to prove that he/she once reminded the employer to conclude a written labor contract with him/her, the claim shall not be upheld.

Plaintiff: Liu Danping, female, 26 years old, domiciled in Jintan City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Nanjing Renchuang Materials Co., Ltd., domiciled at Xinrun Road, Shangfang Jizhen, Dongshan Street, Jiangning District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Tian Kai, General Manager of the Company.

Plaintiff Liu Danping instituted an action in the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, against Defendant Nanjing Renchuang Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Renchuang Company) regarding a labor dispute.

Plaintiff Liu Danping alleged: She commenced work at the Defendant Renchuang Company on March 10, 2015. During her employment, as she was still within the legally prescribed lactation period, Renchuang Company did not approve her daily one-hour nursing break as required by law, and instead extended her working hours through overtime. Renchuang Company failed to sign a labor contract with her from the date of her employment until July 2015, and also maliciously withheld part of her wages. When she proactively communicated with the company requesting the full payment of her wages as agreed, Tian Kai, the legal representative of Renchuang Company, refused and used abusive language. The actions of Renchuang Company seriously infringed upon her lawful rights and interests. Compelled by the above reasons, she terminated the labor relationship between the parties and requested compensation from Renchuang Company, but the parties failed to reach an agreement. She prayed the court to enter judgment: 1. Ordering Renchuang Company to pay the withheld wages of RMB 4,165 for the period from March to July 2015 in full; 2. Ordering Renchuang Company to pay double wages of RMB 11,666 for the period from the commencement of employment due to the non-conclusion of a written labor contract, and economic compensation of RMB 2,917.

Defendant Renchuang Company defended: 1. It did not acknowledge the withheld wages claimed by Plaintiff Liu Danping; the wage records did not show any wage withholdings for all its employees, nor was it aware of such; 2. Regarding the double wages, as Liu Danping was the personnel manager of its company, her basic job duties included matters such as signing labor contracts with employees and other personnel-related tasks; Renchuang Company believed that Liu Danping deliberately failed to sign the labor contract, and thus it did not acknowledge the claim for double wages; 3. It had not defaulted on Liu Danping's wages, and therefore it did not acknowledge the claim for economic compensation. In summary, Renchuang Company requested the dismissal of Liu Danping's claims.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province found at first instance:

Plaintiff Liu Danping commenced work at Defendant Renchuang Company on March 10, 2015, serving as Personnel Manager, primarily responsible for staff recruitment, training, and compensation management. On July 23, 2015, Liu Danping left Renchuang Company and, on the same day, sent a "Notice Regarding the Termination of the Labor Relationship with Nanjing Renchuang Materials Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Notice of Termination") to Renchuang Company, stating that Renchuang Company had failed to sign a labor contract with her, failed to grant her the statutorily required one-hour nursing break during the lactation period, and failed to pay her monthly wages in full, thereby seriously infringing upon her lawful rights and interests; she notified Renchuang Company that the labor relationship would be terminated as of July 24, 2015, and requested compensation.

It was further found that: On July 24, 2015, Plaintiff Liu Danping applied for arbitration to the Jiangning District Labor and Personnel Dispute Arbitration Commission of Nanjing City (hereinafter referred to as the Jiangning District Labor Arbitration Commission), requesting Defendant Renchuang Company to pay the withheld wages of RMB 4,165 for March to July 2015 in full, double wages of RMB 11,666 for the period from the commencement of employment due to the non-conclusion of a written labor contract, nursing break wages of RMB 3,385, and economic compensation of RMB 2,917, totaling RMB 22,133. Since the arbitration application was not concluded within 45 days from the date of acceptance, Liu Danping filed a lawsuit with the people's court. The Jiangning District Labor Arbitration Commission issued an Arbitration Decision (Ning Ning Lao Ren Zhong Cai An Ding Zi [2015] No. 2056) on October 8, 2015, terminating the hearing of the labor remuneration dispute between Liu Danping and Renchuang Company. Thereafter, on October 9, 2015, Liu Danping filed an action in court, requesting Renchuang Company to pay her wages of RMB 4,165 for March to July 2015 in full, double wages of RMB 11,666, and economic compensation of RMB 2,917. Liu Danping submitted a copy of the arbitration application, an original copy of the "Notice of Termination," an original EMS courier waybill, an original copy of the employee application form, and a printed copy of the social insurance payment certificate to support her claims. Renchuang Company did not dispute the authenticity of the above evidence but did not acknowledge the expenses claimed by Liu Danping. It argued that it had paid Liu Danping's wages in full and had not withheld any of her wages. Regarding the double wages, it argued that the reason it did not sign a labor contract with Liu Danping was because Liu Danping, as its personnel manager, deliberately failed to do so; therefore, it did not acknowledge the claim for double wages. Since it had not defaulted on Liu Danping's wages, it disagreed with paying economic compensation. Renchuang Company submitted an original copy of a labor contract and four copies each of the wage records and attendance records for March to June 2015 to prove that it had signed a written labor contract with Liu Danping and had paid her wages in full. Liu Danping did not dispute the authenticity of the wage records and attendance records but pointed out that the wage record for May 2015 clearly showed that wages of RMB 833 had been withheld and not paid. Liu Danping further stated that upon commencing employment, she had agreed with Tian Kai, the legal representative of Renchuang Company, that her annual income would be RMB 70,000, averaging RMB 5,833 per month; however, the actual monthly payment was RMB 5,000, with RMB 833 withheld each month. Therefore, she requested Renchuang Company to pay the withheld wages of RMB 4,165 (RMB 833/month × 5 months) for March to July 2015 in full. Renchuang Company stated that the wage record for May 2015 was prepared by Liu Danping, and that there were no withheld wages for other months; it argued that Liu Danping had maliciously prepared the wage record for May 2015. Liu Danping stated that she had prepared the wage records for both April and May 2015, and that the withheld wage of RMB 833 for May 2015 had been signed and confirmed by the legal representative, deputy general manager, and finance manager of Renchuang Company. Liu Danping disputed the authenticity of the labor contract, arguing that the signature "Liu Danping" at the end of the contract was photocopied rather than handwritten, and applied to the court for a forensic examination. The court lawfully entrusted the Judicial Authentication Center of Nanjing Normal University to conduct the examination. On December 30, 2015, the Judicial Authentication Center of Nanjing Normal University issued a Judicial Authentication Opinion (Nan Shi Da Si Jian Zhong Xin [2015] Wen Jian Zi No. 642), concluding that the three characters "Liu Danping" at the end of the "Nanjing City Labor Contract" dated "March 10, 2015" were formed by laser printing or photocopying, not by handwriting. Liu Danping paid authentication fees of RMB 2,240. Liu Danping stated that after commencing employment, she requested Renchuang Company to sign a labor contract, but Renchuang Company refused; Liu Danping did not submit evidence to support this claim.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province held at first instance:

The lawful rights and interests of employees and employers shall be protected by law. Where a labor relationship is established, a written labor contract shall be concluded. Where a labor relationship has been established but a labor contract has not been concluded at the same time, a written labor contract shall be concluded within one month from the date of commencement of work. Where the employer fails to conclude a written labor contract with the employee for more than one month but less than one year from the date of commencement of work, it shall pay the employee double wages each month. The employer shall pay labor remuneration in full and on time in accordance with the provisions of the labor contract and state regulations. The party who asserts a fact on which its claim is based or who rebuts a fact on which the opposing party's claim is based has the responsibility to provide evidence to prove it. Where there is no evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove the party's assertion, the party bearing the burden of proof shall bear adverse consequences. In this case, a labor relationship existed between the parties. The wage records submitted by Defendant Renchuang Company were sufficient to confirm that Renchuang Company had withheld RMB 833 from Plaintiff Liu Danping's wages for May 2015. Renchuang Company should pay wages in full and on time in accordance with the contract provisions and state regulations. Renchuang Company's defense that the wage record for May 2015 was maliciously prepared by Liu Danping was not supported by evidence and was therefore not accepted by the court. Accordingly, the court partially upheld Liu Danping's claim for withheld wages for the period from March to July 2015.

Regarding Plaintiff Liu Danping's claim for economic compensation of RMB 2,917, although Defendant Renchuang Company did not pay Liu Danping's wages for May 2015 in full, Liu Danping stated during the trial that the withholding of her wages by Renchuang Company was with her consent; Renchuang Company had justified reasons for withholding RMB 833 from her May 2015 wages. Therefore, Liu Danping's claim for economic compensation lacked factual and legal basis and was not upheld by the court.

Regarding Plaintiff Liu Danping's claim for double wages of RMB 11,666, in this case, although Defendant Renchuang Company indeed did not sign a labor contract with Liu Danping, generally speaking, matters concerning the conclusion of labor contracts fall within the scope of human resources responsibilities. As the Personnel Manager of Renchuang Company, Liu Danping's job duties should include acting on behalf of the company to handle matters related to the performance of labor contracts with employees in accordance with laws and regulations, and to avoid the company being held legally liable for violating laws and regulations. She should also have been aware of the relevant provisions on concluding written labor contracts and the legal consequences of failing to do so. Therefore, Liu Danping had the obligation to proactively request Renchuang Company to conclude a written labor contract. However, Liu Danping did not submit evidence to prove that she had once proactively requested Renchuang Company to sign a labor contract with her. After comprehensively considering factors such as Liu Danping's position and responsibilities, the court did not uphold Liu Danping's claim for double wages due to the failure to conclude a written labor contract.

Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 10, Paragraph 1 of Article 30, Item (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 38, Item (1) of Article 46, and Paragraph 1 of Article 82 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Paragraph 1 of Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on March 4, 2016:

I. Defendant Nanjing Renchuang Materials Co., Ltd. shall pay Plaintiff Liu Danping RMB 833 for the May 2015 wages within 10 days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective.

II. All other claims of Plaintiff Liu Danping are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment, neither party appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
